newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin plans jobs without spending rise.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin plans jobs without spending rise.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin will propose an economic policy to boost employment and purchasing power without raising public spending, says a copy of his election manifesto speech published by Le Monde on Friday.

Jospin, whose opposition Socialist Party was due to publish its manifesto later on Friday, would propose a reform of payroll taxes to cut the cost of labour, a shorter, 35-hour working week and creation of 700,000 jobs through a government-backed scheme, the speech said.
The Socialists are also proposing to cut value added tax (VAT) on basic goods and to raise the wealth tax, the speech says.

Jospin also calls for a move to give Europe a political dimension, creating a region focused on growth and unemployment rather than one "founded on deregulation, the end of public services and austerity for the people".

Jospin commits his party, which is trailing in opinion polls ahead of the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, to scrapping the controversial "Pasqua" and "Debre" laws enshrining the ruling centre-right coalition's crackdown on immigration.
